title: Rover on a grid
intro: A rover drives on a grid. Its state is `(x, y, direction)` with direction one of `N`, `E`, `S`, `W`. North is +y, east is +x. The commands are a string of `L` (turn 90 degrees left), `R` (turn 90 degrees right) and `F` (move one cell forward). Use only the standard library. Each level extends the previous one.
rules: Turning never moves the rover. `F` moves it one cell in the direction it faces.
Return tuples `(x, y, direction)` for positions.

levels.title: Run L/R/F commands
levels.prompt: Write `run_rover(start, commands)` for an unbounded grid with no obstacles. It returns the final `(x, y, direction)`.
levels.signature: def run_rover(start: tuple[int, int, str], commands: str) -> tuple[int, int, str]
edgeCases: An empty command string returns the start unchanged
Four R commands in a row return to the same direction

levels.title: Obstacles stop the rover
levels.prompt: The grid is now `width` x `height`, with cells `0 <= x < width` and `0 <= y < height`, and a set of blocked `(x, y)` obstacle cells. Write `run_rover2(width, height, obstacles, start, commands)`. An `F` that would leave the grid or enter an obstacle is ignored: the rover stays where it is and the run continues with the next command. Return a dict with `position` (the final `(x, y, direction)`) and `blocked` (how many forward moves were ignored).
levels.signature: def run_rover2(width: int, height: int, obstacles: set[tuple[int, int]], start: tuple[int, int, str], commands: str) -> dict
edgeCases: Driving off any edge is blocked, not an error
A blocked move still counts as a move attempt, and later commands run normally

levels.title: Several rovers that can't collide
levels.prompt: Several rovers share the grid and the obstacles. Write `run_rovers(width, height, obstacles, rovers)` where `rovers` is a list of dicts `{"start": (x, y, d), "commands": "..."}`. The rovers run in lock-step: in each step number `s` (starting at 0), every rover that still has a command runs its command number `s`, in list order, before the next step begins. An `F` is also blocked when the target cell is currently occupied by another rover. Return a dict with `final` (a list of final `(x, y, direction)` tuples, one per rover) and `blocked` (a list of `(rover_index, step)` for every blocked move, in the order they happened).
levels.signature: def run_rovers(width: int, height: int, obstacles: set[tuple[int, int]], rovers: list[dict]) -> dict
edgeCases: Rovers with fewer commands simply stop early
Two rovers can never end on the same cell
